I have been working in this field for about 5 years. Specifically, I’ve written software to make smartphone batteries last longer for all the recognizable android flagship phones since Samsung Galaxy S7.

First up, most non-smartphones have smaller batteries than smartphones. The legendary Nokia 3315 was something around 1,200 mAH (or 950mAH, I don’t remember). Compare to that, the latest Google Pixel 3 has a 2915mAH battery. The larger phones (iphone Xs Max and Google Pixel 3 XL) have even larger batteries.

The problem is that modern smartphone phone processors draw a lot of current to drive those ridiculously high pixel density displays at 60 odd frames a second.

The changeable battery is a hard one. There are reasons to not allow changeable batteries (better industrial design, physical security inside the device for fingerprint sensors etc, reliable charge-discharge cycles from only known batteries...) but these reasons aren’t important to everyone.

Apple went with the non replaceable battery approach because they wanted those advantages while the initial few generations of android phones decided to go the other way and sell phones with easily replaceable batteries.

Over time, apple was extremely successful with their locked in battery approach while samsung famously had an exploding phone because of a battery problem (I think this was the galaxy s6).

Replaceable batteries was never going to survive that. That’s how everyone ended up with non-replaceable batteries.

I can tell you that the industry is trying really hard to make batteries last longer in a phone. I personally know a ton of really good people working on this. But it takes time. And things will slowly get better with each generation.
